SRE Bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-5 p99 latency spike > 5s for 6m. -> https://pager.link/INC-99321 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: paging Maria K. (on-call)

Alex G.: grabbing this. seeing p95 jump from ~300ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~5.2s, streaming stalls on tail requests. customers hitting dedicated capacity.

Maria K.: on it. I see high queue_depth on pool-5 (queue depth ~780, threshold 200). autoscaler attempted scale but warmup lagged; new nodes created but not ready due to warmup KV sync.

Lucas H.: confirmed logs show warmup TTL for model kv-cache is 45s and CPU-bound init tasks causing handshake delay. here's snippet from runtime logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] pool=eu-west-1-pool-5 queue_depth=782 active=64 warmup_start=2026-03-15T10:11:38Z kv_sync=45.2s handshake=12.4s
[2026-03-15T10:12:08Z] request_id=abcd1234 stage=streaming stall_ms=2200 state=wait_for_kv
```
Tara S.: customer-impact matrix shows 3 mid-market tenants (acct: acme, fastchat, noteflow) saw degraded streaming (partial chunks, stalls) and several 504 client disconnects. CS notified in #customer-success.

Alex G.: root cause hypothesis: dedicated autoscaler created new slots but the warmup path requires KV population from cold stores; the coldpath is throttled -> extended warmup -> queue pile-up -> tail latency spike. autoscaler backoff/health-checks prevented routing until handshake completed.

Maria K.: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily reroute small percentage of traffic from pool-5 to eu-west-1-pool-3 (compatible model variant) 2) manually add prewarmed hotshot nodes with kv snapshot 3) bump autoscaler parallelism to avoid serial warmup. executing now.

Lucas H.: running manual add (redwood-cli):
```
redwood-cli pools scale --pool eu-west-1-pool-5 --add 4 --prewarm true --kv-snapshot=latest
```
SRE Bot: NOTE: manual scale accepted, creating 4 prewarm nodes (ids: pre-772, pre-773, pre-774, pre-775). Expected ready ~40s.

Maria K.: also relaxing route policy to allow degraded variant fallback for 10% traffic to reduce queue. applying policy patch:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/eu-west-1
{ "fallback_allow_pct": 10, "max_queue_depth": 500 }
```
Alex G.: monitoring p95/p99 after actions. initial metrics: p95 -> 560ms (improved), p99 -> 2.3s (improved from 5.2s). queue_depth dropping to 210. streaming stall rate down 80%.

Tara S.: CS update posted: "We're seeing service degradation in eu-west. We've routed limited traffic to backup pool and are prewarming nodes. We're seeing significant improvement; we will follow up with root cause analysis. Apologies for the interruption." cc @customers.

Maria K.: nodes prewarm completed, KV snapshots applied. handshake latency down to ~3s per node; autoscaler parallelism increased.

Lucas H.: observed one node with repeated kv-sync failures due to transient NFS timeout, removed it from traffic: node pre-774 -> cordon/drain.

Alex G.: ramping down fallback after stabilization. Keeping manual prewarm until autoscaler heuristics adjusted (warmup window increased to 70s and parallelism to 3).

SRE Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity reduced to S2. p99 back to 1.0s sustained for 10m.

PagerDuty: paging off Maria K. (on-call) — acknowledged resolved by team.

Maria K.: handing off to ops for postmortem. immediate action items:
- (ops) adjust autoscaler: allow parallel warmups=3, increase warmup timeout to 90s, add kv-snapshot prefetch for hotshot nodes. owner: Lucas H. ETA 48h.
- (runtime) implement faster kv cold-path replication or rate-limit cold-sync to avoid blocking handshake. owner: Alex G. ETA 2 weeks.
- (product) update rollout playbook to include fallback variants for dedicated pools. owner: Tara S. ETA 1 week.

Lucas H.: creating follow-up ticket: https://redwood/ops/INC-99321-followup. I'll include metrics, warmup traces, and node-level logs.

Tara S.: scheduling customer follow-up emails for affected accounts; CS will coordinate message and any credits if warranted.

Alex G.: post-incident notes: this was triggered by a burst of reserved capacity requests + a model KV eviction job that coincided with autoscaler scale-up. The chain was: burst -> cold kv-populate -> slow handshake -> queue pile-up -> p99 breach. Repro steps captured in ticket.

Maria K.: final check: p95=320ms, p99=900ms, queue_depth=38, streaming-stall-rate=0.6%. Marking incident as resolved. Handoff to oncall review. :white_check_mark:

Lucas H.: adding runbook improvements and a short health-check that flags slow kv-sync during scale events. Will pro-rate rollout for multi-tenant pools.

Tara S.: thanks everyone. will own customer comms and postmortem write-up schedule.

SRE Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Incident INC-99321 closed at 2026-03-15T10:16:07Z. Follow-up ticket INC-99321-followup created.
